claims.reason: Backed part: the abstract reports slower and usually more error-prone responses immediately after a task switch (Korzyść i dowody#2). Not backed: the abstract covers experimenter-required switching among a small set of simple tasks, not tasks that demand attention in everyday work, and it does not report that limiting switching improves performance or outcomes. It gives no advice of its own. Searched the whole abstract (ad423624ccd89cce.txt) for advice or for demanding or real-world tasks and found none.

claims.reason: Backed part: avoiding switches is supported only through the switch cost reported in Korzyść i dowody#2 (slower, usually more error-prone responses right after a switch). Not backed: deferring unrelated messages. The abstract does not mention messages, notifications or interruptions; its switches are imposed by the experimenter between simple tasks. It also does not test whether postponing anything improves results. The safety condition 'jeśli możesz to zrobić bezpiecznie' is an editorial caveat with no source. Searched the whole abstract (ad423624ccd89cce.txt).

claims.reason: The grade letter B is editorial and was not checked. The words after it describe the source as a review of research on switching among simple tasks, which the abstract supports. The abstract does not say whether the review is narrative or systematic.

scope_gaps.note: The title speaks of tasks that demand attention and of limiting switching. The abstract measured switches imposed by the experimenter among a small set of simple tasks, and the immediate response cost of a switch. It did not measure everyday tasks or the effect of limiting switching.
The advice concerns deferring unrelated messages in daily life. The abstract says nothing about messages, notifications or self-chosen switching, and measures no outcome of postponing them.

The abstract does not say whether the review is narrative or systematic, how many studies it covers, or whether it pools an effect. The sentence does not claim any of this, but a reader might assume it.

The finding comes from laboratory switching among simple tasks. A reader might assume it applies to complex everyday tasks; the sentence does not say so. The abstract gives no size of the slowdown or of the extra errors.
The abstract names the opportunity for preparation in laboratory switching only. It gives no size of the reduction.
Only the abstract was available, so the claim about the absence of one universal effect size could not be checked against the whole review.
